record.paper_title: Hénon maps: a list of open problems
record.context_brief: saddle and elliptic cycles for H2
record.original_question: Does H2 have both small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles near the origin?

evidence.quote: Question 16. — Does H2 have both small saddle cycles and small elliptic cycles?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the complex Hénon map $H_2:\mathbb{C}^2\to\mathbb{C}^2$ defined by
$$H_2(x,y) = (y,\, x + y^2).$$
The origin $(0,0)$ is a fixed point of $H_2$, and the second iterate $H_2^{\circ 2}$ is tangent to the identity at the origin. A periodic point $p$ of period $n$ (i.e., $H_2^{\circ n}(p)=p$) is called a saddle cycle if the differential $D H_2^{\circ n}(p)$ has one eigenvalue of modulus strictly greater than $1$ and one of modulus strictly less than $1$, and is called an elliptic cycle if both eigenvalues of $D H_2^{\circ n}(p)$ lie on the unit circle (and are not roots of unity giving rise to resonant behavior, in the standard sense of complex dynamics). A periodic cycle is said to be "small" if it is contained in every neighborhood of the origin (equivalently, there exist periodic cycles of arbitrarily large period accumulating on the origin).

Question: Does $H_2$ admit, in every neighborhood of the origin, both saddle periodic cycles and elliptic periodic cycles? Equivalently, do there exist sequences of saddle cycles and sequences of elliptic cycles of $H_2$ accumulating at the origin?
